title: Committable iterator: ergonomic API for resumable, backpressure-aware streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers building robust chat UIs and pipelines need a simple, composable way to consume streaming chat completions while handling partial tokens, function call events, retries, and efficient checkpointing for resumability. Existing SDK iterators leak complexity: users must manage low-level watermarks, persist checkpoints themselves, and implement idempotency/commit semantics on top of the SDK. This leads to subtle bugs (double-processing tokens, lost progress on consumer failure) and poor developer ergonomics.
goal: Design and implement a 'CommittableStreamIterator' abstraction in the Python SDK that: (1) exposes a uniform sync and async iterator surface, (2) provides explicit commit/abort semantics so consumers can mark progress, (3) emits backpressure signals to the runtime so callers can pause/resume ingestion, (4) integrates with SDK retry semantics to guarantee at-least-once or exactly-once processing behavior depending on consumer choice, and (5) ships with examples and tests showing typical UI, batch-processing, and worker patterns.
acceptance_criteria: API: CommittableStreamIterator available on Streaming Chat responses with both __iter__/__aiter__ and a context manager that auto-commits on successful block exit
Checkpointing: SDK persists checkpoints to a pluggable CheckpointStore (in-memory by default, Redis and file-backed adapters included) and resumes from the last committed token offset on reconnect
Backpressure: iterator exposes pause()/resume() and yields 'PAUSE'/'RESUME' signals (or raises BackpressureRequested exception) without losing partial tokens
Retries: integrated with existing request retry middleware so retrying from a failed request resumes from last committed checkpoint and does not re-deliver already-committed tokens
Examples: at least three documented examples (chat UI incremental render, streaming embedders worker, and function-call-first consumer) in the repo docs
Tests: unit + integration tests covering checkpoint persistence, commit/abort semantics, concurrent consumers, and slow consumer scenarios
Telemetry: emit events for commit, abort, resume, pause, and fatal reconnect; add cost/latency tags for investigation
design_notes: High-level design: the CommittableStreamIterator wraps the low-level streaming event source from the runtime and tracks a monotonically increasing 'stream_offset' for each event fragment (partial token, token, function-call-start, function-call-end). Consumers receive Event objects with metadata: type, text (partial/complete), offset, end_of_event boolean. commit(offset) marks durability up to that offset. A lightweight CheckpointStore persists the committed offset per (customer_id, conversation_id). On reconnect or retry, the client requests the runtime to replay from the next offset; runtime supports fast-skip of already-delivered KV-cache states where available.
api_examples:
# sync context manager example:
with client.chat.stream_comittable(model="gpt-xyz", convo=cid) as it:
    for ev in it:
        if ev.type == "token":
            render_incremental(ev.text)
        elif ev.type == "function_call_end":
            handle_function_call(ev)
        
        # commit when a sentence boundary reached
        if is_sentence_end(ev.text):
            it.commit(ev.offset)
# async explicit example:
async for ev in await client.chat.astream_comittable(model="gpt-xyz", convo=cid):
    await process(ev)
    if should_commit(ev):
        await it.commit(ev.offset)
# worker pattern with idempotency: read -> checkpoint -> ack -> process
# ensures acked offsets won't be delivered again on restart
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: We considered a purely automatic checkpointing approach (auto-commit every N tokens or on sentence end) but that hides control from consumers with complex idempotency needs. Alternatively, server-side durable cursors were evaluated but require runtime changes and are less flexible for local-only testing. The Committable iterator keeps control client-side while providing pluggable stores for durability and an API that encourages good defaults (context manager auto-commit on success).

Integration with retry middleware so commit is durable before acknowledging upstream success

testing_plan: Unit tests for offset arithmetic, commit/abort semantics, and race conditions. Integration test that runs a simulated runtime which yields partial tokens and reconnects; confirm consumers resume from committed offset. Load test with slow consumer to validate pause/resume signal prevents OOM. Add property tests for monotonic offsets.

release_notes_draft: Introduce CommittableStreamIterator: opt-in API for resumable streaming chat. Enables commit/abort semantics, pluggable checkpoint stores (file/redis), and backpressure signals. Helps build robust UIs and workers that can resume safely after crashes.
